drivingQuestion: Does one who chews raw wheat recite borei peri ha'adama or borei minei zera'im?
outcomeNote: The clash of sources is resolved as a tannaitic dispute, each source assigned to a different view; no ruling is issued between them.

segments.he: אָמַר מָר: הַכּוֹסֵס אֶת הַחִטָּה מְבָרֵךְ עָלֶיהָ ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה״. וְהָתַנְיָא ״בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי זְרָעִים״! לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְהָא רַבָּנַן. דִּתְנַן: וְעַל יְרָקוֹת אוֹמֵר ״בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה״, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי דְשָׁאִים״.
segments.en: Above, it was taught in the Tosefta that «the Master said: One who chews wheat recites: Who creates fruit of the ground.» The Gemara challenges: «Wasn’t it taught» in a baraita that one who chews wheat recites: «Who creates various kinds of seeds?» The Gemara resolves the problem: This is «not difficult,» as it is the subject of a tannaitic dispute. «This» opinion, that one must recite: Who creates various kinds of seeds, is the opinion of «Rabbi Yehuda, and this» opinion, that one must recite: Who creates fruit of the ground, is the opinion of the «Rabbis. As we learned» in our mishna: «Over» herbs and leafy «vegetables one recites: Who creates fruit of the ground. Rabbi Yehuda says: Who creates various kinds of herbs.» Rabbi Yehuda designates specific blessings for every type of plant, and he certainly distinguishes between vegetables in general and seeds.

moves.summary: No difficulty — the two sources are R' Yehuda and the Rabbis respectively
moves.about: the two sources are two tannaitic views, not one contradiction

moves.summary: Grounds the split in the mishna where R' Yehuda gives vegetables their own blessing
moves.about: a baraita giving borei minei zera'im as the blessing for chewed wheat

edges.cueHe: לא קשיא: הא רבי יהודה, והא רבנן
edges.about: the two sources are two tannaitic views, not one contradiction
the baraita requiring borei minei zera'im over chewed wheat follows R' Yehuda
the Tosefta requiring borei peri ha'adama over chewed wheat follows the Rabbis
the mishna on blessings over vegetables, adduced to ground the split between R' Yehuda and the Rabbis

edges.cueHe: ועל ירקות אומר ״בורא פרי האדמה״, רבי יהודה אומר
edges.about: whether one general blessing covers all produce of the ground or each class of plant takes its own designated blessing
since R' Yehuda assigns each class of plant its own blessing, he will also distinguish seeds from other produce of the ground
